sections.title: Selling skincare online in the UAE, explained honestly

items.title: Aftercare kits: the easiest ecommerce win in beauty
items.body:
The highest-converting product your business will ever sell is the one your therapist just recommended, in the treatment room, to a client whose skin is glowing. Aftercare kits — post-laser, post-facial, post-filler — package that moment into a product with a built-in reason to buy.

Online, the kit keeps working: the booking confirmation links it, the post-visit WhatsApp offers it, and the replenishment flow re-sells it every 6–8 weeks. No cold traffic needed — your calendar is the customer list.

sections.embed:
The operations

Payments, delivery & the UAE checkout reality

UAE ecommerce has its own physics: COD still matters, BNPL (Tabby, Tamara) lifts average order values noticeably, Apple Pay owns mobile checkout, and delivery expectations are same-day-ish in Dubai. A store configured for global defaults quietly leaks local buyers.
We configure for the market: every relevant payment method, courier integration with live rates, click-and-collect (which brings buyers back into the salon — where the next booking happens), and VAT-compliant invoicing from day one.

items.title: Should my salon really sell online?
items.text: If you retail in-store, yes — you already do the hard part (trust and recommendation). The store just removes the limits of shelf hours and shelf space, typically adding 10–20% revenue at retail margins.

items.title: Shopify or WooCommerce?
items.text: Shopify wins on day-to-day simplicity; WooCommerce wins when your main site is WordPress and you want one system. We recommend based on catalogue size, your team and your existing website — both are proven.

items.title: What about products we don't manufacture?
items.text: Most salon stores sell brands they already stock — check your reseller terms, which usually permit it. Kits and bundles of stocked products are the margin sweet spot.

items.title: Is COD still necessary in the UAE?
items.text: Less than before, but yes — a meaningful segment still prefers it, and BNPL (Tabby/Tamara) captures another. Payment breadth is cheap; lost checkouts aren't.

items.title: How do we get traffic to the store?
items.text: You already have it: your booking flow, WhatsApp list, Instagram and post-treatment moments. Flows convert owned traffic first; Google Shopping and Meta catalogue ads scale it later.

items.title: Who handles delivery?
items.text: Integrated UAE couriers with live rates — same-day options in Dubai — plus click-and-collect, which costs nothing and pulls buyers back into the salon where rebookings happen.

items.q: How long until the store is live?
items.a: Ads and the AI booking bot typically produce bookings within 2–4 weeks. SEO compounds over 3–6 months and becomes your lowest-cost channel long term.

items.q: Do we need a big product range?
items.a: No — focused beats broad. Ten well-chosen products and three treatment kits outsell a hundred random SKUs, and they’re far easier to manage.
Your team packs; integrated couriers collect. For low volumes it’s minutes a day; we set up the pick-pack flow and printable labels so it stays that way.

items.q: Can the store connect to our booking system?
items.a: Yes — one customer journey: aftercare kits linked from booking confirmations, click-and-collect that prompts rebooking, and shared customer data where your systems allow.
Platform fees (Shopify/hosting), payment processing, and optional Glowth management for flows and growth. All itemised in the fixed-price scope before you commit.
